claims.text: Degradation diagnosis: beyond vanishing/exploding gradients (addressed by init + normalization), deeper plain nets show higher TRAINING error — an optimization (not overfitting) problem; the constructed identity-mapping argument shows deeper models should do no worse.
claims.context: Full-paper sections 1/3.1/4.1 including Fig.1/Fig.4 plain-vs-residual training curves.

claims.text: Mechanism change: residual reformulation F(x)=H(x)-x with parameter-free identity shortcuts (Eq.1; projection Ws only for dimension matching, Eq.2); bottleneck 1x1-3x3-1x1 blocks for economy; 152-layer net at 11.3 GFLOPs still cheaper than VGG-19.
claims.context: Full-paper sections 3.2/3.3/Table 1; identity-vs-projection ablation (options A/B/C) shows projections inessential.

claims.text: Results: 152-layer single-model 4.49% top-5 val; ensemble 3.57% top-5 test (ILSVRC 2015 1st place); COCO detection +6.0 mAP (28% relative) attributed solely to learned representations; 1st places also in ImageNet detection/localization and COCO segmentation.
claims.context: Full-paper sections 4.1/4.3/Tables 3-5/8 + appendix detection baselines; transfer-to-detection evidence is load-bearing for D02/D03 reuse.

claims.text: What remains missing: 1202-layer CIFAR model trains (<0.1% train error) but tests worse (overfitting without maxout/dropout) — depth scaling has a regularization boundary the paper leaves open.
claims.context: Section 4.2; recorded as the paper's own stated open problem, supporting later pretraining-recipe debates.

limitations.text: Highway-network comparison is concurrent-work framing; later pretraining-recipe readings (DeiT/Swin) qualify architecture-triumphalism.
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

limitations.text: Detection gains use Faster R-CNN baselines of 2015 vintage.
